sources.title: Guttation: A Pressure Relief for Plants
sources.independent_operation: Hydathodes at margins/tips can exude water under root pressure, especially when transpiration is low. This mechanism differs from dew but appearance alone is inconclusive.
sources.governing_conditions_and_exceptions: Unspecified herbs and no leaf/air measurements: a physiological hypothesis, never a case diagnosis. Rare disease associations in the article are not inferred for this bench.

sources.title: Controlling the Greenhouse Environment
sources.independent_operation: Internal horizontal airflow mixes air and canopy conditions; ventilation exchanges greenhouse air. Condensation and humidity depend on the operating environment.
sources.governing_conditions_and_exceptions: Alaska greenhouse guidance and numerical equipment advice are not herb settings. The changed fan may be circulation, exhaust or cooling; its actual role must be established.

sources.title: Greenhouse Ventilation
sources.independent_operation: Condensation is consistent with a surface below air dew point. Air exchange can remove moisture while increasing winter heating demand.
sources.governing_conditions_and_exceptions: Weather, greenhouse, heat and crop assumptions govern rates. No fan setting or promised humidity response is imported into the final.

sources.title: Guidelines for measuring and reporting environmental parameters for experiments in greenhouses
sources.retrieval_extent: Full primary article XML via Europe PMC
sources.independent_operation: Reproducible greenhouse measurements require sensor principle, placement, calibration and spatial/temporal context. Canopy measurements independent of control sensors and reported water-delivery variation support the proposed baseline.
sources.governing_conditions_and_exceptions: Research-reporting guidance, with effort matched to the investigation; it does not prescribe crop operating standards or identify this symptom cause.

sources.title: Measuring the Sprinkler Irrigation Requirement of Container-Grown Nursery Plants
sources.verified_version_or_limit: ENH1197/EP458; exact revision date not displayed in retrieved body
sources.independent_operation: Container water requirement depends on evapotranspiration, canopy capture and distribution uniformity. Repeat weighing can estimate water loss under the guide's stated drainage and timing conditions.
sources.governing_conditions_and_exceptions: Sprinkler nursery context; water delivered is distinct from water retained or consumed. The final uses representative pot mass as a conditional measurement option, not a diagnostic threshold.

sources.title: Field Evaluation of Container Nursery Irrigation Systems: Measuring Uniformity of Water Application of Sprinkler Systems
sources.verified_version_or_limit: FS98-2/AE194; exact revision date not displayed in retrieved body
sources.independent_operation: Catch-can distribution uniformity evaluates spatial sprinkler application; pressure, nozzle, overlap, clogging and wind affect it.
sources.governing_conditions_and_exceptions: An overhead-sprinkler audit is conditional on delivery method. Numerical nursery acceptability thresholds are not adopted as this herb bench's mandatory standards.

sources.title: Irrigation System Check-ups
sources.independent_operation: Inspect operating pressure and emitter consistency; apparently thorough watering can leave dry root balls. Map collected output during an irrigation audit.
sources.governing_conditions_and_exceptions: The final preserves inquiry into actual delivery and wetting. It does not implement the page's repair, cyclic-watering or fertilizer recommendations today.

sources.title: The Use of Soil Moisture Probes for Improved Uniformity and Irrigation Control in Greenhouses
sources.independent_operation: Soil/substrate moisture sensing for irrigation depends on water distribution, root uptake, substrate properties and placement; a sensor may not represent a larger heterogeneous root zone.
sources.governing_conditions_and_exceptions: Abstract supports an optional sensing approach, not a universal threshold, number of probes, automatic saving or validation on unspecified herbs.

sources.title: Implementation of Sensor-based Automated Irrigation in Commercial Floriculture Production: A Case Study
sources.independent_operation: In 2014–2015 Georgia greenhouse geranium/poinsettia trials, grower-controlled sensor irrigation did not reduce water use against historical timer practices. Staff changed thresholds; labor reallocation and support mattered.
sources.governing_conditions_and_exceptions: Peat-perlite, ornamental crops, seasonal trials and grower control differ from this case. Water comparisons were not uniformly replicated. The final reports study history, not a general causal saving estimate.

sources.title: Implementation of Soil Moisture Sensor Based Automated Irrigation in Woody Ornamental Production
sources.independent_operation: The woody-nursery trial reported approximately half the irrigation volume and severe 2015 Rhododendron loss. Authors emphasized crop-specific drought/capture and averaged thresholds. Reported EC did not exceed 2.0 mS/cm, which they considered generally insufficient for damage.
sources.governing_conditions_and_exceptions: Four woody taxa in composted pine bark with overhead irrigation, shade and Georgia weather. Salt discussion does not establish a cause of losses. Final qualification is independently supported by the full PDF, despite the reviser's fresh-access failure.

sources.title: Subirrigation for Greenhouse Crops
sources.verified_version_or_limit: UMass subirrigation factsheet; publication/update date not shown, footer copyright is not an edition date
sources.independent_operation: Subirrigation can reduce overhead leaf wetting and closed systems can reduce runoff; growers report uniformity and less foliar disease. Salt/EC, cleanliness, container zoning and system closure matter.
sources.governing_conditions_and_exceptions: General guidance/reporting, not proof of disease prevention or herb performance. Capillary systems are not necessarily closed. Final keeps this as longer-term feasibility, without selecting installation.

sources.title: Root Diseases of Greenhouse Crops
sources.verified_version_or_limit: UMass root-disease factsheet; exact revision date not shown
sources.independent_operation: Impaired roots can involve abiotic salts or saturation/oxygen limitations and pathogens; visible symptoms are not a unique diagnosis.
sources.governing_conditions_and_exceptions: The final retains environmental and diagnostic branches without assigning a pathogen, prescribing chemicals, or claiming disease prevention.

sources.title: Diagnostics System for Crop History and Disorders in Greenhouses and Nurseries
sources.verified_version_or_limit: UGA Diagnostics System for Crop History and Disorders in Greenhouses and Nurseries; retrieved current text, exact edition date not established here
sources.independent_operation: Chlorosis is compatible with several biotic and abiotic causes. Detailed crop history and accurate symptom terminology help discriminate causes.
sources.governing_conditions_and_exceptions: A diagnostic framework, not a result for this hypothetical greenhouse; its treatment advice is not imported. Supports records, broad differential and referral context.

sources.title: Diagnosing Horticultural Plant Problems
sources.independent_operation: Plant-problem diagnosis uses representative samples, records, signs versus symptoms and possible further testing; multiple stresses can interact.
sources.governing_conditions_and_exceptions: Receiving clinic requirements govern collection. Final refers to local instructions and does not treat photos or the general key as a diagnostic oracle.

sources.title: Pest Management for Herb Bedding Plants Grown in the Greenhouse
sources.verified_version_or_limit: UConn greenhouse-herb guidance; retrieved current page, exact edition date not established here
sources.independent_operation: Herbs vary in moisture preferences: the general drier-media preference has exceptions including basil, parsley and some mints.
sources.governing_conditions_and_exceptions: Unknown species/media prevent adopting a universal drying routine or imported temperature/fertility settings. Final keeps species identity as a necessary owner fact.

sources.title: Basil downy mildew
sources.verified_version_or_limit: University of Minnesota basil downy mildew guidance; retrieved current page, exact edition date not established here
sources.independent_operation: A named basil disease can produce pale/yellow leaf symptoms and additional characteristic signs, illustrating why appearance alone is insufficient.
sources.governing_conditions_and_exceptions: Species is not known to be basil and characteristic signs are not supplied. The final does not diagnose this disease or prescribe the page's disease-management measures.

sources.title: A Wetness Sensor for Detecting Condensation on Tomato Plants in Greenhouses
sources.verified_version_or_limit: Journal of Agricultural Engineering Research 61 (1995); DOI 10.1006/jaer.1995.1047
sources.retrieval_extent: Primary publisher abstract via independent web retrieval
sources.independent_operation: A specific flexible copper/polyamide condensation sensor was tested on tomato fruit surfaces; coatings affected duration agreement.
sources.governing_conditions_and_exceptions: Fruit-surface sensor design and calibration matter. This is not a generic herb-leaf wetness sensor or water-source classifier validation. Direct PDF access was not obtained.

sources.title: Development of a method for condensation rate measurement on flat surfaces
sources.retrieval_extent: Primary publisher abstract via independent web retrieval
sources.independent_operation: Chamber testing calibrated capacitive flat-surface condensation sensing against known condensate under specified temperature and humidity conditions.
sources.governing_conditions_and_exceptions: Controlled flat sensor surface is different from a herb leaf and does not identify guttation or natural droplet origin. Only abstract-level evidence is used.

sources.title: Temperature and Humidity Gradients in Fan Ventilated Greenhouses under Two Cooling Modes
sources.independent_operation: Temperature and humidity gradients were measured in a tall pepper crop under fan-only and fan-and-pad modes and differing ventilation rates.
sources.governing_conditions_and_exceptions: Source discusses specific humidity, not an interchangeable RH value. Final says general humidity gradients and imports no numeric prediction for the teaching greenhouse.

sources.title: Wireless sensor network to map the meteorological variability in a greenhouse with evaporative cooling
sources.independent_operation: A Brazilian evaporative-cooling/shading greenhouse study mapped configuration-dependent horizontal and vertical environmental variability.
sources.governing_conditions_and_exceptions: Site, crop, climate, cooling, shade and control configuration constrain transfer. Supports mapping, not a claimed door benefit or prescribed fan schedule.

sources.title: Measuring Nursery Plant Water Use in Containers
sources.verified_version_or_limit: Virginia Tech container-water guidance; retrieved current web text, exact edition date not established here
sources.independent_operation: Container evapotranspiration depends on weather, crop stage, substrate, spacing and root/canopy mass; repeated weighing can inform water-use inquiry.
sources.governing_conditions_and_exceptions: Final does not execute or prescribe the source's wilt-point experiment; its baseline is observational and any stressed plant stops a later comparison.

sources.title: Pseudoreplication and the Design of Ecological Field Experiments
sources.retrieval_extent: Primary Wiley/ESA publisher abstract; independently downloaded scanned reprint also retained
sources.independent_operation: Inferential treatment comparisons require independently replicated treatments; multiple samples from one treatment unit do not supply treatment replication.
sources.governing_conditions_and_exceptions: Ventilation assignment must be independent at zone level; plants are nested samples. The SCW multi-zone counterfactual does not refute that principle. Scanned reprint had no extractable text; no claim of full-text reading is made.

sources.title: How to Avoid Common Problems with Leaf Wetness Sensor Installation and Maintenance
sources.verified_version_or_limit: UF/IFAS AE538; retrieved current text, visible body lacks edition date
sources.independent_operation: Conventional leaf-wetness sensors respond to electrical/dielectric changes and record wetness duration; installation and maintenance affect signal.
sources.governing_conditions_and_exceptions: An ordinary duration signal is not a label of dew, irrigation or guttation. Field-specific mounting prescriptions are not universal greenhouse instructions in the final.

sources.title: Identifying the Source of Water on Plant Using the Leaf Wetness Sensor and via Deep Learning-Based Ensemble Method
sources.retrieval_extent: Primary IEEE publisher abstract via independent web retrieval; Crossref identity metadata also retained
sources.independent_operation: The tested ensemble combines wetness-pattern/frequency information with temperature, relative humidity and duration to classify dew, rainfall and irrigation.
sources.governing_conditions_and_exceptions: A separately trained model is distinct from a basic logger. Neither abstract nor final establishes guttation recognition, herb transfer or validation at this facility; no headline accuracy is imported as a facility guarantee.

sources.title: Phytophthora nicotianae transmission and growth of potted kalanchoe in two recirculating subirrigation systems
sources.retrieval_extent: Primary ScienceDirect publisher abstract and record
sources.independent_operation: In inoculated Kalanchoe tests, contaminated nutrient solution yielded pathogen recovery in both tested recirculating systems but differing disease expression; media-inoculation transmission depended on system.
sources.governing_conditions_and_exceptions: Nutrient-flow wick versus ebb-and-flow, named host/pathogen and inoculum route. Supports conditional contamination risk and exceptions, not universal spread or a herb diagnosis.
